references.text: The first month of the year was established as the beginning of Israel's religious calendar, providing context for the time mentioned in Exodus 40:17.
Refers to the same day Moses completed setting up and anointing the tabernacle, confirming the event described in Exodus 40:17.
Describes the Passover celebration in the first month of the second year, during the same period as the raising of the tabernacle.
God's original command to build the tabernacle (mishkan) so that He could dwell among His people, now fulfilled.
Detailed instructions for constructing the tabernacle, now realized in the setup described in Exodus 40:17.
God's command to Moses to raise the tabernacle on the first day of the first month, now carried out.
The tabernacle is described as a shadow and type of heavenly things, showing the typological significance of its setup.
Describes the structure and furnishings of the earthly tabernacle, with reference to the tabernacle raised in Exodus 40:17.
This shows the transition from establishment to journeying: the tabernacle is completed in the second year (Exod), and the cloud lifts to move on later that same year (Num).
This verse describes the divine response (cloud/fire) immediately after the tabernacle was raised in the source verse.
Creates a theological arc from the wilderness tabernacle to Jerusalem's temple by linking both moments to the Exodus from Egypt.
